name: Christian humanism
summary: Christian humanism holds that human dignity, learning and freedom find their fullest foundation in Christian faith. Its Renaissance form (Erasmus, Colet) sought church and social reform through classical and biblical scholarship and peace among Christian princes; its twentieth-century political form (Maritain's integral humanism) defends natural rights, democracy and pluralism while rejecting both totalitarianism and secular humanism.
scope: Mainly the twentieth-century personalist strand, Jacques Maritain's 'integral Christian humanism' (with Mounier's circle), supplemented by the Erasmian northern Renaissance strand on peace, princes and reform. Excludes secular humanism, Italian Neoplatonic humanism's courtly strands, and confessional integralism. The ideology is partly a philosophy of the person, so economic and many modern-issue answers are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Jacques Maritain

universal-healthcare.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's stress on workers' rights, the common good and the dignity of every person; the sources do not discuss healthcare itself.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the personalist concern for workers' rights and a just livelihood; no source addresses wage floors directly.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Maritain rejected both socialism and tying Christianity to capitalism, and subordinates economy to the common good, so an unqualified market claim is unlikely; inferred.

public-ownership.rationale: Maritain avoided socialism, though he did not demand pure private ownership either; inferred that wholesale public ownership is not a core commitment.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the common-good orientation of property and solidarity with workers; the sources give no tax position.

unions-good.rationale: Maritain's defence of workers' rights and of civic fraternities and intermediate bodies implies support for free workers' associations.

property-fundamental.rationale: Personalists treat property as subordinate to the common good rather than as an absolute right; inferred from natural rights being oriented to the common good.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from the primacy of the common good and the person over economic gain; sources do not address corporate regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from solidarity and concern for the poor in Christian ethics and Maritain's rejection of liberal individualism.

worker-ownership.rationale: Adherents are split: personalists have favoured worker participation and co-responsibility, but Maritain avoided committing to socialist ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the inviolable dignity and conscience of the person, which cannot be subordinated to the state; the sources do not discuss surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred; Christian humanism has no stated drug policy and its moral emphasis on the whole person leans against, though not strongly.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents divide between protecting freedom of conscience and expression and protecting dignity from degradation; no source settles it.

strong-leader.rationale: Maritain broke with Action Francaise over its anti-democratic nationalism and rejected fascism; the person may not be subordinated to a leader.

state-harmful.rationale: Maritain holds the state is a necessary instrument of the common good and treats authority as natural, so anarchism is foreign to it.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split and the tradition has no distinct position on firearms.

empower-police-military.rationale: Erasmus condemned militarism and warmongering princes, and personalism limits state coercion; inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the Christian moral framework and concern for human dignity; not addressed directly in the sources.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on every person's dignity and transcendent destiny; sources do not discuss penal policy.

traditional-family.rationale: Christian moral framework typically treats the family as foundational; not stated in the sources opened, so inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The classical and Catholic-influenced Christian humanist tradition has held traditional marriage; modern strands differ, so inferred and low.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the inalienable dignity of the human person grounded in natural law; sources do not address abortion directly.

more-religion-public.rationale: Maritain envisioned a Christianly inspired polity in which religion and civic fraternities have a leading role, while pluralist and non-coercive.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's opposition to antisemitism and defence of equal dignity; remedial policy itself is not addressed.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred; a Christian anthropology of the whole person leans against treating gender as purely constructed, but the sources do not address it.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Humanists valued cultural inheritance, yet Erasmus and Maritain looked past nation toward Christian and human unity; split.

gradual-change.rationale: Northern humanists such as Erasmus pursued reform through education and learning, not rupture; inferred as a general temperament.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from universal human dignity and Christian hospitality; no source addresses immigration levels.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Maritain supported a world federation of political societies and championed the Universal Declaration, provided states keep fair autonomy.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; economics subordinate to the common good and adherents are split.

nation-first.rationale: Erasmus calls national hatreds artificial and urges Christians to unite as one; Maritain favoured wider federation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Erasmus condemned nearly all war, while later Catholic just-war thinking allows defence of the innocent; adherents split.

open-borders.rationale: Universal dignity favours generous treatment of migrants, but Maritain envisaged states keeping autonomy, so open borders is not endorsed; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: No stated position; the integral humanism is concerned with human flourishing rather than growth limits, so inferred mild disagreement.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Modern strands (including stewardship theology) lean in favour but classical sources are silent; split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Maritain argued that a humanism lacking the spiritual dimension is merely partial, so technical progress alone cannot save humanity.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; no basis in the principles for a clear call.

revolution-justified.rationale: Maritain sought a pluralist, democratic and non-violent renewal and rejected communist revolution; Erasmus abhorred violence; inferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: Maritain held that authority derives from the people and their natural right to govern themselves.

central-planning.rationale: Maritain rejected communism and socialism and held the person cannot be subordinated to the state.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; Maritain was neither a socialist nor a capitalist and the question is open.

land-value-tax.rationale: No position; outside the tradition's concerns.

tax-inheritance.rationale: No stated position; common-good limits on property cut one way and family and property for persons the other.

basic-income.rationale: No stated position; adherents split between solidarity with the poor and concern for work and responsibility.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from the subsidiarity-like preference for intermediate bodies and rejection of state-dominated economies.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Personalist and Christian social thought favours property distributed among persons, but the sources opened do not state it; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Maritain rejected communism, whose aim this describes.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition has no anarcho-capitalist leanings.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Maritain valued intermediate bodies and fraternities but opposed state domination, so state-recognised wage-setting finds mixed support.

one-party-rule.rationale: Maritain rejected fascism, communism and all totalitarian rule and affirmed democracy and pluralism.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Erasmus addressed princes and accepted monarchy as given, whereas Maritain defended democracy; split.

democracy-best.rationale: Maritain argued that democratic self-government is consistent with the Gospel and championed democratic pluralism (s2); the Erasmian strand in scope addressed princes and did not argue for democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Maritain defended representative democracy where leaders express the people's will; direct law-making is not a stated aim.

workers-councils.rationale: Maritain rejected communism and worked within a pluralist democratic order, not rule by councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common view.

natural-rulers.rationale: Maritain held that authority arises from the people and equal dignity of persons; rule is not a natural prerogative of some.

political-violence-never.rationale: Erasmus came near pacifism while the Thomist tradition accepts just war and resistance; adherents split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Erasmus calls war the worst of evils, contrary to nature and religion, and a calamity borne by the common people.

separate-church-state.rationale: Maritain proposed cooperation between church and state, each with its own sphere, rather than strict separation, while rejecting a confessional state.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Maritain grounds law in natural law known by reason and accessible to all, within a pluralist polity, not direct scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state is an instrument of the common good and justice is a public matter in this tradition.

military-superiority.rationale: Erasmus opposed arms rivalry and war and Maritain backed world federation; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Maritain opposed nationalism and affirmed the universal dignity of the person, and Erasmus held national hatreds artificial.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Maritain rejected Marxist communism and Christian humanism stresses cooperation and the common good.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Equal dignity is central but the sources do not support equalising outcomes; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Erasmus urged Christian unity across kingdoms, whereas Maritain pointed to a wider world federation; split.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Personalism and Christian ethics treat the person as oriented to the common good and to love of others.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Maritain held that persons cannot be subordinated to society and that natural rights are inalienable and prior to the state, while also stressing duties.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Christian creation theology can affirm it, though humanism centres on persons.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from the dignity of each person and the Catholic-influenced tradition; sources do not address.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Maritain called for a new Christendom, not a rejection of modern civilisation; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Christian humanism prizes learning, culture and the classical heritage, which are incompatible with this.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from the integral view of the person as a spiritual whole; sources do not address transhumanism.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Government is human self-rule and moral judgement in this tradition, so handing it to algorithms is alien.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from the claim that a purely secular progress is partial; no direct statement.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; person-versus-state privacy leans one way and public order the other.

restore-past-order.rationale: Maritain's new Christendom was explicitly not a return to medieval order but a new pluralist form; inferred.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Maritain grounded politics in natural law and principles rather than pragmatic outcomes alone.

direct-action.rationale: Maritain favoured democratic and civic means and Erasmus reformed through learning and persuasion.

means-match-ends.rationale: Erasmus argued that Christian ends cannot be served by violence and war; inferred as a general ethos.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A Marxist aim that the tradition rejects.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not stated; solidarity with the needy sits against respect for work and property.

production-for-use.rationale: Not addressed; the common-good priority is shared, but this is a socialist formula.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Maritain rejected Marxism and its theory; Christian critique of abuses does not equate all profit with exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Maritain rejected communism and totalitarian dictatorship in favour of democratic personalism.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivisation belongs to communism, which Maritain rejected.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a Christian humanist doctrine; Erasmus blamed princely ambition and hatreds, and Maritain rejected the Marxist analysis.

taxation-theft.rationale: Maritain holds the state serves the common good and authority is legitimate, so taxation is not theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Maritain held that law is tied to natural law and the common good, which can reach beyond preventing harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights belong to persons but the person is social and oriented to the common good, and Maritain recognised workers' and other associational rights.

conscription.rationale: Erasmus opposed war while Thomism accepts defensive service; split and not addressed.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Maritain held that the people's right to govern themselves is the heart of legitimate authority.

state-as-business.rationale: The state serves the common good, not customer satisfaction.

positive-liberty.rationale: Maritain recognised workers' rights and integral human flourishing, implying freedom needs material means; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: Neither Erasmian nor Maritainian sources make any claim about media or university power, so adherents are genuinely split.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Maritain affirmed the equal dignity of all and denounced racism and antisemitism.

organic-representation.rationale: Maritain valued civic fraternities and intermediate bodies but within democratic representation; split.

total-state.rationale: Maritain rejected fascism and communism and held that the person cannot be subordinated to the state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Maritain broke with the nationalist Action Francaise and rejected fascism.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Erasmus condemned wars over dynastic claims and borders as the greatest evil.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Maritain grounded authority in the people, not in personal oaths of fealty.

bound-labor.rationale: Maritain's personalism holds that the person is never a mere instrument of another (s2), which excludes serfdom; no cited text discusses bound agricultural labour itself.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Christian humanists recovered classical learning in the confidence that truth can be recovered through philology and reason.

universal-morality.rationale: Maritain's natural law holds that universal first principles exist and can be recognised by all.

single-common-good.rationale: Maritain treats the common good as the basis of the state, yet he also defends a pluralist polity of differing convictions (s2), so how far adherents reject interest-balancing is contested.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; Maritain defended Jews against persecution but the sources opened state no position on Israel.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The tradition has no stated view on diaspora return or citizenship rights; nothing in the sources supports a side.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is a nationalist concern that Christian humanism, oriented to universal Christian culture, never took up.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from personalist emphasis on workers' participation and rights; sources do not state it.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from Catholic and Christian preference for parental choice and Christian education; not stated in the sources.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is outside what Erasmus or Maritain addressed, and adherents hold varied economic views.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not addressed; Maritain did not tie Christianity to capitalism.

rule-by-example.rationale: Erasmus stressed the prince's example and wisdom but also law and arbitration, and Maritain relied on democratic institutions; split.

national-self-determination.rationale: Maritain supported popular self-government but also federation; the claim about each nation's right to a state is not addressed.

force-without-un.rationale: Maritain supported international institutions and a world federation; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Christian humanism holds faith and reason as complementary and rejects the exclusive reliance on reason that defines secular humanism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from universal dignity of persons.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between solidarity and responsibility.

class-collaboration.rationale: Personalism is a via media between individualism and socialism and rejects class struggle in favour of the common good.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Christian humanism is defined by recovering classical and patristic heritage and learning.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western fronts are a postcolonial project absent from Christian humanist sources, so no position follows.

workers-nation.rationale: The national-versus-international organisation of labour is a socialist debate this tradition did not engage.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred; modern Christian humanism favours equal rights in law, even where traditional family views persist.

ban-interest.rationale: Medieval prohibitions on usury were not carried into modern Christian humanism; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Maritain opposed racist persecution and held all persons equal in dignity (s4); racial segregation law is not discussed directly in the cited texts.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Maritain rejected Marxism and holds the state serves the common good.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production is an anachronistic question for this tradition, with no principled lean in the sources.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Maritain's pluralism accommodates differing conscience and culture; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiratorial claim at odds with Maritain's opposition to antisemitism and his humane stance.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system design is not discussed by Maritain's democratic theory in the sources opened, so adherents are split.

national-mission.rationale: Erasmus condemned national hatreds and chauvinism; inferred.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents split.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Erasmus and Colet did criticise corrupt clerics and princes, but a general populist charge is not a core claim.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Maritain's claim that every person has an inalienable dignity grounded in God (s2) excludes state control of who may have children; eugenics is not discussed in the cited texts.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from the primacy of natural rights and law over state power.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Maritain assigned the state a positive role in the common good and workers' rights.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Maritain wrote against racism and antisemitism (s4), and his equal dignity of persons leaves no ground for discouraging mixed marriages; mixed marriage itself is not discussed.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equal dignity of persons and inalienable natural rights are central to Maritain's personalism and to the Universal Declaration he championed.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate foreign to the tradition; Maritain rejected socialism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The sources do not address settler-colonial analysis, and adherents differ on how to classify such states.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; Maritain's pluralism accommodates religious conscience, so split.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Maritain stressed freedom of conscience and a pluralist polity.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Maritain's cooperative church-state model and Christian pluralism leave room for religious instruction in schools; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Maritain argued that authority derives from the people, who have a natural right to govern themselves.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade aims are not addressed by Christian humanist sources; no stated position.

population-transfer.rationale: Maritain's rights of the person (s2) protect members of minorities as persons, which rules out expelling them as a group; forced transfer is not discussed directly.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Erasmus came near to this, but the Thomist tradition allows just coercion by the state; split.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Erasmus holds that humans were made for mutual aid and condemns strife.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Maritain defended pluralism, yet opposed totalitarian movements; split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed; neither affirmed nor rejected.

separated-powers.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's democratic constitutionalism and belief that authority is limited by natural law.

vanguard-party.rationale: Maritain rejected communism and Leninist party rule in favour of pluralist democracy (s2); the vanguard thesis itself is not discussed directly.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Christian ethics and Maritain's solidarity with workers imply concern for the poor, though the sources opened do not state a formal priority.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing-policy question never addressed by the tradition; no stated position.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Christian social thought locates poverty in institutions and moral failure; inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Maritain's pluralism holds that people of differing convictions can cooperate on shared practical aims.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not endorsed; Maritain favoured elected representation.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Rights are inalienable and prior to the state in Maritain's natural-rights thought.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price regulation is not discussed in the sources; the tradition's concern for the poor and its caution on state economics pull in opposite directions.

party-controls-media.rationale: Maritain rejected totalitarian states and defended freedom of conscience and expression (s2), which rules out party control of the press; media control is not discussed directly.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation periods are a technical question outside the sources, so adherents are split.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Legislator pay levels are not addressed in the sources opened; no principled lean.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on personal conscience that persons cannot give up to organisations.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Maritain proposed a world federation of political societies that retain a fair degree of autonomy; pooling of sovereignty fits.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Christian humanists differed by confession (Catholic and Protestant); split.

clerical-rule.rationale: Maritain's polity is pluralist, with church and state in distinct spheres (s2), so clergy holding supreme political power is excluded; clerical rule is not discussed directly.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist doctrine alien to the tradition.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on freedom of conscience and the humanist love of learning and literature.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from the democratic and constitutional emphasis.

recall-officials.rationale: Maritain's sources discuss democratic authority but not recall mechanisms, so the answer is genuinely open.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Maritain supported international order and cooperation; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Contradicts the tradition's moderation and rejection of collectivist schemes; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Erasmus opposed war and militarism; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Christian humanism was an urban, scholarly movement and did not romanticise rural life, nor attack it; no stated view.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is a question of nationalism the tradition did not address.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Christian humanism prizes learning as a path to piety and reform (s1), which disposes adherents against anti-intellectual claims; whether graduates are out of touch is not discussed.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Natural law is universal, but Maritain's pluralism respects cultural difference; split.

death-penalty.rationale: Catholic-influenced adherents split; the tradition has historically allowed but modern strands oppose.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Christian humanism values learning and reason, so mixed religious science in schools is not favoured; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the moral emphasis on dignity of the person.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from universal dignity and opposition to ethnic nationalism.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's pluralism and respect for differences.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Maritain stressed freedom of conscience and accommodation of differing religious conscience.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's individualism contrasts with personalism's emphasis on community and the common good; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt policy is not addressed by Erasmus or Maritain in the sources opened; adherents differ.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A dependency-theory claim absent from the tradition, which has no stated view on it.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making procedure is not addressed in the sources, though democratic legitimacy is valued; left neutral.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Maritain rejected authoritarian rule and holds rights inalienable.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from the Christian duty of solidarity and universal human dignity.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Erasmus condemned war and arms; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Executive selection methods are institutional details outside the sources opened.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not addressed by the tradition; no position can be inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Erasmus urged settling disputes by arbitration and avoiding war over territory; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Maritain held natural rights are oriented toward the common good, and Christian social thought treats property as having a social function.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Maritain simply rejected the Soviet system; the technical debate is not addressed.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is modern and not addressed, with no principled lean in the sources.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed directly; Maritain backed international cooperation but Erasmus opposed war.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Erasmus condemned conquest and border redrawing without regard for the people governed.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Maritain proposed cooperating church and state, each in its own sphere, and rejected totalitarian control.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The ceremonial-head model is not addressed; Erasmus wrote to active princes and Maritain on democracy generally.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Erasmus condemned war over territory; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special-autonomy arrangements are not discussed in the sources, though Maritain valued pluralism; left neutral.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Maritain held authority derives from the people; Erasmus addressed princes as fallible and obliged to serve the people.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax-rate structure is not addressed by the tradition; no basis for a lean.

character-from-environment.rationale: Christian humanism stresses both moral education and an innate nature and soul; inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is an anachronistic topic with no treatment in the sources opened.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-government theory is not discussed in the sources opened, so the answer is neutral.

leader-cult.rationale: Maritain rejected fascism and any subordination of the person to a leader or the state (s2), which rules out leader veneration; public leader cults are not discussed directly.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court presumptions are a modern legal detail the sources do not address.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis foreign to the tradition.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform is not discussed in the sources opened; Christian social concern for the poor and respect for property split adherents.

refugee-return.rationale: Return rights in particular conflicts are not discussed in the sources opened; adherents differ.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Contradicts Maritain's anti-nationalism and Erasmus's condemnation of conquest.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Maritain defended freedom of conscience in a pluralist polity of believers and unbelievers (s2), which excludes legal penalties for leaving a faith; apostasy law is not discussed directly.

women-must-cover.rationale: State compulsion of this kind contradicts freedom of conscience.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; supports international union but not directly.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Ethnolinguistic unification is a nationalist aim not found in Christian humanist sources.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's pluralism and civic fraternities.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to equal rights and Maritain's defence of persecuted Jews, whom he helped to leave but also defended in place.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A Marxist thesis that Maritain's spiritual integral humanism rejects.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred from the primacy of the common good over concentrated economic power.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is a modern economic question the sources do not address.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Maritain held natural rights are inalienable and prior to society, so majorities cannot override them.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not addressed by the tradition, and adherents differ on them.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Erasmus emphasised unity among Christians and nations; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's emphasis on workers' rights and international cooperation.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; moral motive is valued but not as a replacement.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Erasmus condemned war and violence (s3) and Maritain rejected revolutionary violence, so guerrilla vanguard strategy runs against both strands; the strategy is not discussed directly.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Curriculum framing is not addressed in the sources, though Christian humanists did centre classical and Christian heritage; left neutral.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from the equal dignity of all peoples and persons.

patriotic-education.rationale: Erasmus distrusted national hatreds, whereas modest loyalty could be accepted; split.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action policy is not addressed by the sources; adherents differ between remedying injustice and colour-blind equality.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not addressed by the tradition in the sources opened.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Whether capitalism can avoid collapse is a Marxist-framed question the sources do not engage.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred from the stress on international cooperation.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis foreign to the tradition.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Maritain's equal dignity of persons and his denunciation of antisemitism (s2) cut against a right to refuse service on group grounds; private discrimination law is not discussed directly.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Maritain held rights are inalienable and championed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Legal status of colonial treaties is not addressed by the sources opened.

elective-rulers.rationale: Maritain held authority derives from the people.

minority-veto.rationale: Maritain valued the role of dissenting minorities but accepted majority democracy.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Maritain held that positive law contradicting natural law is not true law, which supports resistance to lawless rule.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not addressed; natural law limits any lawmaker.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred; Christian humanism accepts concern for suffering though centred on persons.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from the person-centred view that allows use of animals with compassion.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Erasmus urged princes to govern for the people and Christian duty binds the privileged to the needy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Maritain developed a politically engaged integral humanism and Erasmus urged learned engagement in reform.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Frankfurt-school claim; Christian humanist sources do not take a position on it.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is not engaged by the tradition, so no answer follows from the sources.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not addressed by Erasmus or Maritain in the sources opened.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from equal dignity and rights of citizens.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist-movement question that Christian humanism, which rejects communism, does not engage.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is not addressed in the sources, and solidarity-minded adherents are split.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Erasmus opposed war to recover territory; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to equal political rights.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Maritain rejected fascism and its nationalism and supported democracy.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Maritain rejected both fascism and communism as inhuman.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to equal human dignity.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument controversies are not addressed by the tradition, which values heritage but also equal dignity; left neutral.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents differ on how to treat gendered disadvantage.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed by the sources opened; adherents differ.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Maritain held rights and democracy universal but accommodated pluralism; split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's democratic constitutionalism and Erasmus's anti-militarism.

paid-care-work.rationale: Recognition of domestic work as paid labour is not addressed in the sources; adherents are split.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from Christian moral tradition (honour thy father and mother); sources do not discuss.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service recruitment by exam is a Confucian-style question the tradition did not address, though it prizes learning.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Industrial policy on foreign ownership is not addressed in the sources.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the Christian view of marriage; adherents vary.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Not endorsed; Maritain's democracy is representative, expressing the people's will through leaders.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not addressed by the tradition, with no principled lean in the sources.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from the defence of natural rights including property and rejection of collectivism.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget control is not discussed in the sources opened, though democratic authority is supported; left neutral.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign land ownership is not addressed by the sources opened.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Legal doctrine on indirect discrimination is not addressed in the sources; adherents differ.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Maritain held that a humanism lacking the spiritual dimension is partial, and Christian ethics criticises acquisitiveness.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Erasmus condemned wars of domination and Maritain backed international law.

decide-locally.rationale: Maritain valued civic fraternities and intermediate bodies and accepted federation, so local decision-making is welcome but not a stated principle; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Erasmus holds princes must govern for the people and Maritain holds that positive law contradicting natural law is not true law.

corporate-influence.rationale: Maritain's personalism criticised capitalism's domination of persons by money, but he did not address lobbying specifically; inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Maritain's pluralism and anti-totalitarianism favour open civil society, while sovereignty concerns are not discussed; inferred as neutral.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Catholic social teaching and Maritain's concern for the family favour supporting families, though the sources do not state it; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Personalism values free movement and Erasmian cosmopolitanism cuts against local residency barriers; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Maritain defended workers' dignity and rights, but a job guarantee is not a stated position and adherents differ on state employment schemes; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Erasmus and Maritain both prized peace and Maritain defended democracy, so spreading democracy for peace fits their outlook; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Maritain grounded law in natural law, so unjust laws lose moral force, but he still held that just law binds the conscience and rejected a general disclaimer.

non-intervention.rationale: Maritain backed world federation and universal human rights, which imply that outside action in cases of grave abuse can be legitimate; Erasmus condemned war but not all outside involvement.

industrial-unions.rationale: Christian democratic and personalist circles supported unions and workers' participation, but industrial against craft form is not addressed; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Maritain opposed antisemitism and defended pluralism, so he rejected conspiracy theories against minorities.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Christian humanism treats marriage as a sacrament and a social foundation of the person, so it opposes abolishing it as a legal institution.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Maritain's democratic personalism favours open and accountable government; the sources do not discuss information rights, so this is inferred.

local-production.rationale: Distributist and personalist strands favour local economy, while Erasmus's cosmopolitan Europe favoured open exchange; inferred as split.

informal-organisation.rationale: Maritain defended institutions, pluralist associations and democratic order, not only informal small groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Maritain defended a world federation and universal rights above the state, and Erasmus decried narrow national interests, so national law over international is rejected.

religious-nation.rationale: Maritain's pluralism rejects a state defined by one religion, and he favoured a democratic order in which people of different beliefs cooperate.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Erasmus condemned princely ambition and Maritain backed a federated order of equal peoples; ritual tribute to a leading power is inferred as foreign to both.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from the personalist emphasis on the common good and solidarity, which favours sharing across regions.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Maritain defended private property as a natural right yet limited it by the common good; the sources opened do not settle where he draws the line for productive property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Maritain rejected atheistic communism and totalitarianism but is not known for a doctrine of defeating it; Erasmus predates communism. Inferred as split.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Maritain's pluralism and subsidiarity favour a range of independent bodies serving the common good within a framework of public concern.

religion-illusion.rationale: Christian humanism holds that human dignity is founded in faith, so it rejects the view that religion is only consolation that fades.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Maritain criticised both liberal individualism and collectivism, so a judgement on capitalism as a progressive stage is inferred as split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the personalist focus on moral and legal dignity of the person over systemic economic analysis; confessional strands differ.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from Christian stress on the family and subsidiarity, which prefers care within families and communities over state services.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Erasmus's humanism prized learning across languages and Christian unity over national hatreds, so purging foreign words is inferred as opposed.

treaties-binding.rationale: Maritain's natural-law and rights outlook, and Erasmus's stress on good faith, support honouring agreements; no source addresses internal nations directly.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Maritain's pluralism favours many associations within a state, not reorganising society into communal-property communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's pluralism, rights and opposition to antisemitism, which are opposed to steering majority settlement into minority regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Maritain's integral humanism rejects both liberal individualism and totalitarian collectivism and seeks a different, personalist order.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Maritain's personalism gives every person equal dignity and rejects blood-and-soil claims; inferred, as the sources do not address land claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Integral humanism defends the dignity of every person and opposes totalitarian ideologies, so denying such a crime has no place in it; this is implied rather than stated.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from traditional Christian sexual ethics tempered by Maritain's defence of civil rights and pluralism; the sources do not discuss it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Maritain defends democracy, natural rights and pluralism and rejects totalitarianism, which rules out suppressing opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Maritain's pluralist political order rejects confessional integralism, which the scope excludes, so the state should not punish false religion; inferred from his pluralism.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from the personalist emphasis on dignity and Erasmus's critique of ruling for princely gain; colonies are not discussed.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Erasmus's Complaint of Peace and Maritain's stress on peace make an absolute religious duty of war unlikely; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Maritain defends democratic legitimacy and Erasmus condemned violent rebellion and war; inferred from those commitments.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the personalism of Maritain and Mounier's circle, which stresses the person's active role in community life.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Adherents would oppose racism and defend workers' rights, but the sources do not take a view on whether these must be tackled together.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from traditional Christian anthropology that most adherents hold, although the twentieth-century sources do not discuss gender identity.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from the Christian view that human life is sacred and its dignity belongs to every person; the sources do not mention assisted dying.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Maritain's third way draws on both sides, but adherents do not claim left and right are obsolete; split and inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred from the personalist critique of treating workers as mere means, which Maritain and Mounier raised against capitalism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's pluralism and the universal dignity of persons; the sources do not discuss Islam.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Maritain holds that authority comes from God through the people; the sources are summaries and do not state it in these words, so this is inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Maritain's pluralism and religious liberty suggest tolerance of religious dress; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from the defence of human dignity and natural rights; workplace law is not discussed.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's call for a personalist economy that serves the common good, between laissez-faire and statism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred from Erasmus's pacifism, set against Maritain's acceptance of defence as legitimate; neither calls for abolition.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the common good and equal dignity of persons, which resist deliberate inequality; not discussed.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Erasmus urged peace among princes, while Maritain backed the democracies in the twentieth century; no statement on blocs, so inferred and split.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's defence of democracy and the equal dignity of persons; hereditary succession is not discussed in the sources.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Personalism stresses workers' and communal institutions but the sources say nothing about mutual banking, so no direction is inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses sovereign debt or the IMF, and Christian humanists are split on it.

property-franchise.rationale: Maritain grounds democracy in the equal dignity and natural rights of every person, which rules out wealth qualifications for voting.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The personalist tradition does not treat the two forms of domination as one; adherents differ and the sources are silent.

reification.rationale: Inferred from the personalist critique of treating persons as things under materialist economics; the sources do not use this concept.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Maritain defends civil liberties and also criticises the power of money, but the sources do not address media ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Maritain's natural-law politics holds that rulers are bound by law grounded in justice, and that arbitrary decrees are not true law.

racial-franchise.rationale: Maritain's natural rights belong to every person as a person, so an ethnic franchise contradicts the core doctrine.

online-participation.rationale: A twentieth-century strand that never addressed the internet; no direction can be inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's democratic ideal of an informed public and accountable rulers; open data is not discussed.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Maritain's pluralism treats people of differing faiths as equals who cooperate, so legal bars on interfaith marriage are inferred to be rejected.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Maritain's equal dignity of persons and cooperation across religious convictions rule out singling out a minority for shunning.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's defence of democracy and the dignity and participation of the ordinary person; the sources do not discuss sortition.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Erasmian humanists returned to scripture and the fathers over scholastic authority, while Maritain defended Thomism; the strands split, so no clear position is inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's stress on the common good and the dignity of workers against domination by economic power.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Maritain and Erasmus never addressed it and modern Christian humanists are divided; no position is inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Maritain rejects totalitarianism and secular humanism and defends religious freedom and pluralism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Maritain's natural-law politics accepts a legitimate state with coercive justice; abolition is inferred to be rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's pluralist democracy, in which communities and groups have their own place within the political body.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Maritain's Christian democracy supports state action for justice alongside voluntary charity; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Not discussed in the sources and no principle clearly decides it.

vote-delegation.rationale: Maritain defends representative democracy; delegable voting is inferred to be outside his model.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred from the stress on human dignity and Erasmus's warnings against destructive war; the issue itself is not discussed.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Christian humanists are split by denomination, and the Catholic Maritain tradition and Protestant strands differ.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from personalism's equal dignity of persons; the sources do not discuss marital authority.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Maritain's pluralism favours broad participation, but the sources do not address it and adherents are split.

rent-control.rationale: Maritain stresses the common good, but the sources do not address rent regulation.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from Catholic personalism accepting private property with a social function, not abolishing patents.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's personalist rejection of totalitarianism, including regimented state youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from Erasmus's condemnation of war in The Complaint of Peace.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred as split: peace emphasis but acceptance of defensive alliances.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from the dignity of every person and Maritain's defence of human rights.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's stress on workers' dignity and critique of capitalism.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Maritain accepts just war and self-defence while Erasmus condemns war, so adherents mostly reject an absolute ban.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from the universalism of Christian humanism and Erasmus's critique of national rivalry.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the natural-law personalism of Maritain; the sources do not address it.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred as above; the sources do not address feminist theory.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Erasmus criticised glorifying war, and martyrdom is reserved for faith; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Maritain distinguishes the spiritual from the temporal and aims at a pluralist civic order, not politics as holy war.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The sources do not address diaspora and adherents have no common line.

culture-before-state.rationale: Erasmian reform worked through learning and moral renewal before politics; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Tradition mostly keeps male language for God but also holds God beyond sex; adherents are split.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Maritain defended women's dignity but the sources do not address this test; adherents are split.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Maritain's rights-based pluralism rests on the equal dignity of every person, rejecting economic dominance by a majority.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from the pluralist, personalist outlook; the sources do not address it.

independent-unions.rationale: Maritain's pluralism favours free intermediate bodies; inferred, with no direct statement on unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Integral humanism rejects Marxist collectivism while favouring workers' participation; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: No documented position; adherents vary between pluralist public and private provision.

second-chamber.rationale: Maritain's pluralist democracy values checks and plural representation; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: The strand favours personal property and plural forms of ownership rather than communal ownership; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Maritain favoured world federation and pluralism, but nothing is documented on non-governing confederal councils.

family-wage.rationale: Christian social thought supports a just family wage; inferred from the tradition.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; no position can be inferred.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed; human dignity supports research but adherents are cautious of life-extension aims.

person-over-state.rationale: Maritain's personalism holds that the person is never merely a means to the community or state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Integral humanism rests on human dignity grounded in faith and a spiritual end beyond politics.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Maritain's pluralism and subsidiarity give intermediate bodies their own rights; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed; no position can be inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; no position can be inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Maritain defended universal rights and opposed antisemitism, rejecting politics organised by race.

racial-pride.rationale: Erasmus condemned national hatreds, but ordinary pride in ancestry is not addressed; inferred.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Erasmus's Complaint of Peace condemns war among Christian princes.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Maritain's personalism values particular cultures but grounds the political community in the common good, not language; inferred, not discussed in the sources.

communal-electorates.rationale: Maritain's pluralist democracy rests on equal citizenship of persons whatever their beliefs, so confessional separate electorates are inferred to be disfavoured.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Nothing in the sources frames foreign plots against the nation; Maritain's and Erasmus's internationalist, peace-seeking outlook suggests rejection.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's stress on the dignity of every person and on education and learning as goods; free tuition itself is not discussed.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from the common-good emphasis and stewardship of creation in Christian thought; taxation of pollution is not addressed in the sources.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the common good and the Christian view of the Earth as entrusted to humanity; the sources do not state it.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Personalism stresses the equal dignity of persons and does not single out women's distinct values; adherents are not clearly one way.

arms-reduction.rationale: Erasmus's Complaint of Peace condemns war and princely armament and urges peace among Christian princes; the modern reading with a national-safety floor is inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Erasmus's call for peace through arbitration and Maritain's democratic values suggest openness in diplomacy; secret treaties are not discussed.

capital-controls.rationale: Maritain and Erasmus never addressed capital movements and a committed adherent could go either way.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's view that the state holds legitimate authority for the common good; not discussed directly.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Erasmus condemns war between Christian princes as unchristian, which supports refusing to fight them; Maritain accepted just war, so this is inferred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Maritain defended workers' rights and free association as part of the dignity of the person and the common good.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's stress on the common good and justice for workers; tax credits are not discussed.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition's emphasis on the common good pulls both ways.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's call for a more just social order and concern for the poor; not discussed for the world economy.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Maritain rejected totalitarianism and revolution and defended a pluralist democratic state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Maritain favoured pluralism but also a defined personalist, communitarian economy; adherents are split.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; inferred as neutral.

sacred-nation.rationale: Maritain distinguished nation from state and rejected idolising either, so calling the nation sacred is inferred as disagreement.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from concern for the common good and access to education; not discussed directly.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; inferred as neutral.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Maritain grounded human dignity and natural rights in a common human nature given by God; this is central to his humanism.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from the stress on pluralism and public goods; not discussed directly.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Maritain held that the Christian faith is the fullest truth and defended pluralism without relativism, so the claim that all religions express one truth is rejected.

farm-price-support.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the common-good and workers' dignity emphasis.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Maritain and Erasmus stressed peace, but deterrence in a world of rivals was not addressed in the sources; split, so neutral is inferred.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Christian-democratic strand backs workers' rights through broad cross-class parties rather than a class party; inferred from Maritain.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; protecting the dignity and bodily integrity of the person is inferred from personalism.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Maritain's equal dignity of every person implies equal rights for women; the sources do not discuss property, so inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The ideology did not address language; neutral is inferred.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not addressed; Maritain favoured a pluralist state with regulation for the common good, so tort-only is inferred to be disliked.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Maritain defended democracy and natural rights under constitutional law, so an official role for customary chiefs is inferred to be unwelcome.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Care for creation fits Christian humanism but the sources never rank it against liberty; neutral is inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Erasmian and personalist emphasis on the person and mercy suggests preferring judicial discretion; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; Maritain's pluralism and universal dignity pull against a compulsion, so neutral is inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Maritain backed workers' associations and a personalist economy but the strands never addressed compulsory dues; inferred and split.

voter-id.rationale: Maritain defended democracy and the rights of the person but nothing in the sources addresses ballot identification; adherents could go either way.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Maritain's pluralist state lets people of different creeds cooperate on common goods without enforcing one creed; inferred for interpretations within a religion.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Maritain grounds democracy in natural rights and the dignity of the person, so it requires moral substance beyond fair elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Maritain's Catholic personalism upholds traditional sexual morality; inferred, since the sources focus on political philosophy.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's defence of natural rights including freedom of expression and from Erasmus's scholarly openness; the question is anachronistic.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The personalist economy favoured by Maritain is not tied to a specific welfare design; inferred and split.

women-suffrage.rationale: Maritain's defence of equal natural rights and democracy implies equal political rights, though the sources do not discuss suffrage directly.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Christian humanism holds that Christian faith is the foundation of human dignity, so it would deny religion is a main cause of oppression; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Maritain opposed racism and racial theories as contrary to the unity of the human person; inferred for the scientific claim.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: No source addresses state machinery for equality; Maritain's pluralism and subsidiarity pull in opposite directions, so adherents would be split.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's view that property serves the common good and the universal use of goods; the sources do not discuss first-claim ownership.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from Erasmus's plea for peace among princes and Maritain's call for a wider political community; the sources do not discuss criminal courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from Erasmus's philological, critical reading of the Bible and Maritain's Thomism; the sources do not address inerrancy directly.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the personalist emphasis on the equal dignity of every person; the sources do not discuss Indigenous self-government.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's rejection of totalitarianism and collectivism; the sources do not discuss defending planned states.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's defence of democracy and popular participation; indirect election is not discussed.

national-church-status.rationale: Maritain's pluralist democracy and defence of religious freedom point against a privileged legal position for one church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's personalist pluralism, which values the autonomy of intermediate communities; autonomy for ethnic minorities is not discussed.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the personalist stress on consent and human dignity; the sources do not discuss plebiscites.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed; Erasmian concern for peace might favour stable borders while personalism favours self-determination, so adherents could go either way.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the Erasmian and Christian ideal of modesty and moderation; simple self-sufficient living is not an explicit theme in the sources.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's universal human rights and freedom of movement; the sources do not discuss settlement.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed; peace-minded Erasmian humanism leans against conscription while equal-dignity personalism favours equal treatment, so no clear answer.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Maritain defended the nation as a natural community but not a mystical land bond; the question is not discussed and is inferred.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Maritain grounds natural rights and the dignity of every person in Christian faith, so killing without trial is rejected.

close-ties-china.rationale: Christian humanism had no position on China versus the United States; inferred as neutral.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Erasmus's Complaint of Peace urges peace among Christian rulers over national causes; protecting co-nationals abroad is inferred as not endorsed.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Maritain accepts the universal destination of goods, so common claim on resources is inferred; the compensation idea is not discussed.

self-ownership.rationale: Maritain's personalism separates the person from the individual and stresses duties to the common good, so full self-ownership is inferred as rejected.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The sources do not discuss consumption taxes; inferred as no position.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Maritain backed workers' rights and the common good but the sources do not address targeted versus universal spending; inferred.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Maritain defends pluralist democracy and intermediate bodies and rejects totalitarian leader rule, so bypassing parties and groups is rejected.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Maritain's stress on the common good and justice implies against special privileges for the well-connected; inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Maritain rejects a confessional state yet backed Christian-inspired political action, so adherents are split; inferred.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Maritain's integral humanism seeks a new Christian civilization that embraces modern progress while keeping Christian roots; inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Catholic Maritain accepted the church's view of marriage as indissoluble, though Erasmus allowed divorce in cases; inferred and split.

national-resource-control.rationale: The sources do not discuss resource ownership; inferred as no position.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from Christian teaching that goods are meant for all, which Maritain's humanism shares; the sources do not discuss distribution directly.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed; adherents could either welcome a levy on speculation or favour other measures.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred from Maritain's stress on the equal dignity of every person, which treats racial injustice as a continuing wrong.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Maritain's natural-law personalism holds that law gets its authority from justice, in the tradition that an unjust law is no true law.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from the personalist stress on the dignity of work and persons; the question is anachronistic for the sources.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred: Maritain favoured stronger international institutions, which is closer to the disagree side.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the tradition values labour's dignity but has no labour theory of value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred: Christian humanism values both the national community and the dignity of working people.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: the personalist tradition values both economic justice and cultural and spiritual life, and does not rank one clearly first.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Maritain defends democracy and pluralism and rejects totalitarianism, so a communist-party-led system is opposed.

missingStatements.text: Peace among nations should be pursued by arbitration rather than war, and wars of princely ambition are never justified.
missingStatements.rationale: Erasmus urges settling disputes by arbitration and condemns dynastic wars as the worst of evils.
missingStatements.declined: Arbitration over war is a narrow peace-politics view; empower-international-orgs and political-violence-never do not match it closely enough.

missingStatements.text: Human rights are grounded in a natural law that exists independently of any government's decrees.
missingStatements.rationale: Maritain bases inalienable natural rights on natural law and holds that contrary positive law is not true law.

missingStatements.text: People who disagree about religion and ultimate beliefs can cooperate on shared practical aims in a pluralist society.
missingStatements.rationale: Maritain developed a theory of cooperation across differing convictions in a pluralist polity.
missingStatements.declined: Pluralist cooperation is near-universally endorsed, so it would not be contested; separate-church-state and equal-moral-worth cover its substance.

notes: Renaissance and modern strands differ: Erasmus addressed princes within monarchy, while Maritain defended democracy. Confessional differences (Catholic and Protestant) split moral issues; most answers on economy and modern controversies are inferences. Sources opened did not address economics or property in detail.
